answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because willow only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, knoll is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any forge approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
